answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it can submit orders, then slash that bond when independent auditors reproduce a fraudulent claim. Creating a thousand identities no longer multiplies influence for free: each must tie up capital and expose it to loss. A mirror may reflect the same operator, but it still needs its own bond; zephyr-speed account creation and sable-colored profiles cannot evade the economic cost.
